introduction: On this Sunday, the Book of Wisdom tells us that God loves everything he has made and spares all things because they are his. In the Gospel, Zacchaeus, a rich tax collector, climbs a tree to see Jesus, and Jesus says, Today I must stay at your house. Zacchaeus changes his life, and Jesus declares that the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost. Let us welcome Jesus into our homes and our lives.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is good to all, and his compassion is over all his works. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may seek out the lost with the love of Jesus, who called Zacchaeus by name. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are despised or rejected by others: that they may know that Christ wants to stay with them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the rich and powerful: that, like Zacchaeus, they may share their goods with the poor and repair any wrong. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are searching for God, even from a distance: that Jesus may see them and call them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may receive Jesus joyfully and let him change our lives. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you love all that you have made. Your Son came to seek and save the lost. Call us by name, come into our homes, and make us generous as Zacchaeus was. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Today salvation has come to this house
reflection.body:
The Book of Wisdom marvels at God's patience with his creation: "you have mercy on all men... and you overlook the sins of men to the end that they may repent." And it gives the reason: "For you love all things that are, and abhor none of the things which you made." God does not hate what he has created. He corrects us "little by little," so that we may turn back to him.

The Gospel shows that patient love in action. In Jericho lives Zacchaeus, "a chief tax collector, and he was rich." Tax collectors were seen as traitors and cheats. Zacchaeus wants to see Jesus, but he is short and the crowd is in the way. So this wealthy man does something undignified: he runs ahead and climbs a sycamore tree.

When Jesus reaches the spot, he looks up and calls him by name: "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house." Zacchaeus hurries down and welcomes him "joyfully." The crowd grumbles that Jesus has gone to stay with a sinner.

Then Zacchaeus stands and makes a promise: "Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much." No one demanded this. Being loved by Jesus changed him. And Jesus says, "Today, salvation has come to this house... For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost."

Zacchaeus was looking for Jesus, but Jesus was also looking for him. Jesus found him first.

This week, let Jesus call you by name. Is there something that keeps you from seeing him? Climb your own tree: make an effort to meet him in prayer. And if there is a wrong you need to set right, do it, as Zacchaeus did.
